comment.body: Thanks for confirming that mouse input still works and that Task Manager does not need to be always on top. This matches the cursor-visibility investigation in #51542, which also has normal/elevated comparisons and reports from Services, PowerShell and CMD. Please keep this always-on-top counterexample with that investigation; another diagnostic ZIP is not needed to establish the grouping. The privilege-dependent root cause is not confirmed yet.

fix_assessment.rationale: Existing51542 is the active covering investigation, not an implemented or shipped fix.

known_information: The report supplies0.102.3001, an archive and reproducible CursorHide/administrator Task Manager steps.
The discussion explicitly links51542. Latest participant says the cursor becomes invisible over Task Manager regardless of always-on-top, remains operational, and returns after Alt+Tab.
51542 supplies a normal/elevated comparison and reproduction with elevated PowerShell, Services and CMD; no confirmed root-cause repair is established.
issue_context.summary: Route elevated-window invisible-pointer reports to51542, retaining the new evidence that always-on-top is not required.
initial_investigation: Read full report and all three replies, plus the complete51542discussion and latest elevated-CMD confirmation.
Checked current AutoHideCursorWorker activity-hook and cursor-restore paths; no elevated runtime reproduction or archive-derived root-cause claim is made.
inferences: The normal/elevated contrast supports a privilege-sensitive visibility investigation but does not prove UIPI, always-on-top or a particular hook API is the root cause.
issue_context.analysis: The reports describe cursor visibility rather than lost mouse input. Existing51542 is the concrete covering investigation. Always-on-top alone is contradicted by the latest test, while privilege-sensitive activity observation/restoration remains a hypothesis.
